blocks.text: + The Communal Award was announced by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald on 16th August 1932. It is also known as MacDonald Award.
+ It recognised the "Depressed Classes" as minorities and provided them a separate electorate along with some other communities like Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Europeans, and Marathas as well.

+ Mahatma Gandhi strongly opposed the separate electorate for Depressed classes, viewing it as a threat to Hindu unity however B. R. Ambedkar supported the Award, as it ensured political representation and safeguarded the rights of the Depressed classes. Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Communal Award.
Poona Pact 1932
The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar, signed on 24th September 1932, at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune.

While in prison, Gandhi announced a fast unto death till the time separate electorates were removed from the Award, which led to an agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar that discarded the separate electorate.

Gandhi's Efforts against Untouchability
All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932): This League, founded by Mahatma Gandhi was later re-named as the Harijan Sevak Sangh.
Harijan (Weekly newspaper).
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1935
1937 Elections
Congress formed ministries in all 7 out of 11 provinces (later 8) except in:
Bengal: Krishak Praja Party + Muslim League coalition.
Sindh: United Party (Coalition).
For provisions of GOIAct 1935 refer to chapter: "Important Acts" in Polity section.
1934: Congress Socialist Party was formed by J PNarayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, A N Dev, Minoo Masani.
1936: Held in Lucknow; All Indian Kisan Sabha (AIKS) was formed by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.

1937: Faizpur — 1st session to be held ina village (Jalgaon, Maharashtra). This session was presided over by J L Nehru, + 1938: Haripura, Gujarat led by S C Bose (elected as President of INC) marked the beginning of growing ideological differences between Bose and Mahatma Gandhi, though the full rift developed in 1939 during the Tripuri Session.
National Planning Committee (NPC) was established in 1938 by S C Bose, during the Haripura Session. The first chairman of this Committee was J L Nehru.

+ 1939: Tripuri Session in Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) > S C Bose was re-elected as President of INC by defeating Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but later S C Bose resigned from Congress and he formed All India Forward Bloc, 1939 in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh (as a faction within the Congress).
In 1939, World War II began —> It was fought between the Allied Powers (Britain, France, USA, USSR) and the Axis Powers (German, Italy, Japan).
In October 1939, the INC resigned from all provincial ministries to show protest against Britain's decision to involve India in World War II without consulting Indian leaders.
After resigning, the INC made offers to Viceroy Lord Linlithgow regarding India's involvement in World War II.
The demands were:
1. Demand for establishment of Constituent Assembly to draft a Constitution for the Indian people.
Demand for establishment of fully responsible Government at both Provincial and Central level.
Autobiography of Hitler: Mein Kampf
The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as the "Day of Deliverance" (Youm-e-Najat) to celebrate the resignation of the Congress governments.
AUGUST OFFER 1940
+ In 1940, August Offer was sent by Lord Linlithgow under the direction of British Prime Minister Winston Churchill to secure India's cooperation in World War II. The key Provisions were:
1. The British Government promised to grant Dominion Status for India.
2. Indians could create their own Constituent Assembly themselves with inclusion of more Indian representatives than whites.
3. An advisory war council was to be established.
4.Veto for Minorities: No future constitution would be adopted without the consent of the minorities.
iy However these provisions were rejected by Congress as Congress had declared "Purna Swaraj"' as their goal.
Jawaharlal Nehru completely rejected the British August Offer of 1940, calling it "dead as a doornail".
The Muslim League also rejected this proposal.
Individual Satyagraha 1940

+ The INC decided to launch the "Individual Satyagraha" after the failure of August Offer under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi in 1940 with Vinoba Bhave nominated as first Satyagrahi, J L Nehru as second and Brahma Dutt as the third.

Objective: To protest against India's forced participation in World War II and to assert the right to freedom of speech, without causing mass disruption to British war efforts, · Revolutionary Socialist Party was established in 1940.
CRIPPS MISSION 1942
Background/Reasons (1941):
+ Threat of Japan: Rapid Japanese expansion in Southeast Asia and advance up to Burma created fear of invasion of India.
International Pressure: After the Pearl Harbor attack, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Allied nations pressured Britain to grant political concessions to India.
Attack on Russia: Operation Barbarossa by Germany against the Soviet Union (1941) worsened Britain's war position, increasing its urgent need for Indian support (men and resources).
In 1942, Stafford Cripps was sent to India witha constitutional reforms. The key proposals were:
1. A Constituent Assembly would be formed to frame a new constitution for the country. This Assembly would have members elected by the provincial assemblies and also nominated by Princely States.:
. India would be granted Dominion Status, allowing self-governance while remaining part of the British Commonwealth.
. Any province unwilling to join the Indian dominion could form a separate union and have a separate constitution.
. The transfer of power and the rights of minorities would be safeguarded.
The proposals were rejected by INC. Gandhi famously referred Cripps offer of Dominion Status as "post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank".
+ July 1942: The Congress Working Committee met at Wardha, Maharashtra where Quit India Resolution was adopted. It was ratified at Gowalika Tank, Bombay.

On 8th August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi launched Quit India Movement (also known as August Kranti) in response to the failure of Cripps Mission. Which was initially not supported by J L Nehru and Hindu Mahasabha.

The "Do or Die" slogan was given during a speech by Mahatma Gandhi at the Gowalia Tank Maidan or August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai. The slogan was a call to action for Indians to fight for independence from British rule.
+ The very first day all leaders got arrested and that is why this movement was a leaderless movement.
+ Aruna AsafAli presided over Congress Working Committee, she also hoisted the Indian Flag at the Gowalika Tank in Mumbai.
Specific Appeals made by Gandhi (during the Quit India Movement):
To government servants Gandhi advised not to resign from their posts but instead urged them to remain loyal to the cause of the INC and work against British policies subtly.
Soldiers were instructed not to resign from their duties but were urged to refuse orders to fire on fellow compatriots.
Gandhi appealed to peasants to withhold rent payments if the landlords or Zamindars were loyal to the British government.
He encouraged the people living in princely states to support their ruler if the ruler was anti-British. If the ruler was pro-British, Gandhi advised them to peacefully oppose the government.
Kushal Konwar was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged.
Kanaklata Barua was shot dead by the British forces while leading a procession during QIM.
Underground Activities Carried Out:
Usha Mehta: Launched underground radio in Bombay and appealed Indians to join Quit India Movement
Parallel government were setup: In Ballia by: Chittu Pandey
—— In Tamluk by: Jatiya Sarkar
In Satara by: Prati Sarkar (Y B Chauhan, Nana Patil)
23 March 1943: Pakistan Day was observed by Muslim League.
Jinnah's Reaction:
Due to disagreement (especially with Gandhiji's Non- Cooperation Movement), Jinnah left the Congress for some time and went to London.
Upon returning to India, he reorganized the Muslim League and finally stuck to the demand for a separate nation as Pakistan through the Lahore Resolution of 1940.
The word "Pakistan" was coined by Rahmat Ali in 1933.
Lahore Resolution (1940):
It is also called the Pakistan Resolution.
+ It was a formal political statement adopted by the All India Muslim League on the occasion of its three-day general session in Lahore, Punjab, from 22 to 24 March
A separate homeland for the Muslims of British India was demanded.
On 23 March 1943 Pakistan Day was observed by the Muslim League.
Mediation between Congress and Muslim League e 1944: C. Rajagopalachari gave C R_ Formula (Rajagopalachari Formula) in response to the growing tensions between the INC and the Muslim League.
Desai_Liaquat Pact 1945: It was an unsuccessful agreement between Bhulabhai Desai (from Congress) and Liaquat Ali Khan (from Muslim League).

1945: Wavell Plan was proposed by then Viceroy Lord Archibald Wavell as an attempt to resolve the political deadlock between the INC and the Muslim League. This plan was discussed in Shimla Conference; however it failed.

In September 1945, World War II completely ended with the US bombings. In August 1945, US bombed in Hiroshima and Nagasaki (two cities of Japan) on 6 August and 9 August respectively. The bomb dropped on Hiroshima was known as "Little Boy". While the bomb dropped on Nagasaki was known as "Fat Man" which was more powerful than the "Little Boy" and that is from where we came up with the idea of naming this book and our GK MCQ Book (Little Boy).

It was initially formed in 1942 by Mohan Singh with Indian Prisoners of Wars in Singapore (it was later handed to Rash Behari Bose who again transferred the Bir as Z epaery Of oC Base leadership to S C Bose). ie. celetrated seucryniyesy as Subash Chandra Bose

The Indian National Army (Azad Hind
Fauj) was reorganised by Bose in Singapore in 1943.
He founded "Free India Legion/Tiger pasion anon al Berlin, Germany.
He formed a women regiment named after Rani Lakshmibai led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan.

+ 14 April 1944, Colonel Shaukat Ali Malik of the Azad Hind Fauj (INA) hoisted India's tricolor flag in Moirang, Manipur, with the help of Japan. (This was the first time the tricolor was hoisted on Indian soil by the Azad Hind Fauj.)
On 15th August, Japan (Emperor Hirohito) surrendered to Allied powers, marking the end of World War II.
He died on: 18th August in a plane crash.
SC Bose was called as "Patriot of Patriots' by Gandhi.
In 1944, he was the person to give "Father of Nation" title to Gandhi through Singapore Radio.

The Indian National Army trials (also known as the INA trials and the Red Fort trials) was the British Indian trial by court martial of a number of officers of the Indian National Army (INA) between November 1945 and May 1946.
First INA trial was held against: Prem Kumar Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in Red Fort in 1945.
Congress came in defence of these INA soldiers and formed a committee which included Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, Asaf Ali, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, and others.
18th February 1946: The ratings (sailors in lowest rank)

of Royal Indian Navy (RIN) revolted against British due to the discrimination and poor conditions and this led to a historic Royal Indian Navy Mutiny. This event began at the HMIS Talwar (a shore establishment in Bombay) and spread to Calcutta, Karachi and Bombay, against the poor working conditions (low pay, poor food quality, etc.).
The mutiny was called off at the behest of the Congress and the Muslim League.
In 1945, elections were held in Britain where Labour Party under the leadership of Clement Atlee formed the government.
In March 1946, Clement Attlee (then PM of Britain) sent a delegation called the Cabinet Mission consisting of:
Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Chairman), Sir Stafford Cripps and A, V. Alexander.
182 - MODERN HISTORY
Objective: Transfer of power and constitution-making.
Provisions in Cabinet Mission Plan + The plan proposed a united India, rejecting the demand for a separate Pakistan.
The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed a_ three-tier administrative structure for British India:
~ Federal Union at the top level, - Groups of provinces at the middle level, ~ Individual provinces at the bottom level.
Provincial were divided into three groups:
—— Group C: Bengal and Assam.
+ Central Government to have power over defense, foreign affairs, and communications.
+ Provinces to have full autonomy and residual powers.
Princely States were free to negotiate their status, either to join with Britishers or Successor Governments.
Constituent Assembly to draft a new constitution; members would be elected by provincial assemblies.
Interim Government to function till the new constitution and government were formed.
Note:

Attlee's Declaration: On 20 February 1947, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced in the House of Commons that the British government intended to transfer power to responsible Indian hands before 30 June 1948.
Response to the Cabinet Mission Plan + Indian National Congress: It accepted the plan partially but opposed the idea of grouping, fearing it was a step toward partition.

Muslim League:- It initially accepted the Cabinet Mission Plan, despite no explicit provision for Pakistan, hoping that the grouping of provinces would eventually lead to a separate state. However, when Muhammad Ali Jinnah realized that grouping was not strictly mandatory, he called for "Direct Action Day" (16 August 1946) demanding Pakistan, this led to horrific communal violence in Calcutta, known as the "Great Calcutta Killing."
Noakhali Riots (Oct-Nov 1946) in Noakhali (now in Bangladesh) began after the Calcutta violence. Mahatma Gandhi visited Noakhali to establish peace.

The Mountbatten Plan which formed the basis for Indian Independence Act proposed for the Partition of India into two Dominions namely India and Pakistan. That's why it is also known as Partition Plan.
Under this Plan, the Princely States were given the option to join either India or Pakistan or remain Independent.
Out of 565 Princely States, 562 joined either India or Pakistan and 3 did not join initially. They were:
J&K, Hyderabad and Junagarh.
Lord Louis Mountbatten: The last Viceroy of British India and the first Governor-General of independent India (1947-48).
+ C. Rajagopalachari: Only Governor-General of independent India (because later this post was removed).
Note: To see Provisions of Indian Independence act 1947 refer to chapter "Important Acts" in Polity section.

Operation Polo (September 1948): Also known as the Hyderabad Police Operation. This operation was led by Major General J.N. Chaudhuri. The Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, surrendered on 17 September 1948, after which Hyderabad became a part of India.
Maharaja Hari Singh signed the "Instrument of Accession"
on 26 October 1947, officially making Jammu and Kashmir a part of India.

Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (Hindu Mahasabha): He was a strong supporter of 'Akhand Bharat' (Undivided India) and an opponent of partition. He was not formally a leader of the RSS, but Godse considered him his political guru. eSipsla House Incident: On 30 January 1948, at Birla House in Delhi, during the evening prayer, Nathuram Godse touched Gandhiji's feet and then assassinated him by firing three bullets.

Reason for Assassination: Godse believed that the partition of the country happened due to Gandhiji's non- violence and Muslim appeasement policy. (Immediate Cause was the release of *55 crore to Pakistan by the Indian Government due to Gandhiji's fast).
Execution: Tried at the Red Fort, Nathuram Godse and his accomplice Narayan Apte were hanged in Ambala Jail on 15 November 1949.
Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971 led to the separation of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) from West Pakistan (now Pakistan). This war took place during the tenure of Indira Gandhi.

In 1972, the Shimla Agreement was signed by Indira Gandhi (then Prime Minister of India) and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto (then President of Pakistan) to restore peace between two countries. It has been suspended by Pakistan as a move of retaliation after India suspended Indus Water Treaty =.
